<!--
Add an entry for each food safety control of your own that the pack does not cover, and for each
special process you use, such as sous vide. Copy the lines from "## OWN-01" down, paste them below
this comment, number the entries OWN-01, OWN-02 and so on, and write each entry's name after its
number. Kind is additional or special-process.
An entry of kind additional needs Hazard, Control, Check and If-it-fails, and leaves Process empty.
A Limit needs a Limit-source: where the figure comes from.
An entry of kind special-process needs Process, Supplied-text and EH-review. Process names the
special process or food the entry covers, as the profile asks about it, and is one of these:
Vacuum packing; sous vide; low temperature cooking; fermenting; smoking or curing meat/fish; Kebabs; sushi/sashimi; liver parfait; fish/meat carpaccio and tartare; less than thoroughly cooked burgers.
Supplied-text is the business's own written procedure, kept exactly as it is written. Start each
line after the first with two spaces: whatever follows them is kept, further spaces included, and
so is a blank line between two such lines.
EH-review is pending, or the date and outcome of the council's review, such as 2026-11-03 accepted.
To carry any other value on to more lines, start each extra line with two spaces, straight after
the line before it, with no blank line between.
State says where an entry stands: unanswered (it may hold what has been given so far; By and On stay empty);
proposed (taken from a file, or given without a name, and not yet agreed by a named person at the business: say where it came from in Source);
or confirmed (given or agreed by a named person at the business: put their name in By and the date, as YYYY-MM-DD, in On).
Only a confirmed entry goes into your documents: any other is named there as not yet confirmed.
The names of the special processes and foods are quoted from the Food Standards Agency's Safer food, better business for caterers, retrieved 17 November 2026. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

## OWN-01 Opened milk for coffee

Kind: additional
Process:
Hazard: Milk going off once the carton has been opened.
Control: Write the date on each carton when it is opened, and keep open cartons in the drinks fridge.
Limit: Use by the end of the day after the carton is opened.
Limit-source: The dairy's label says to use opened milk within 2 days; our own rule is shorter.
Check: Staff check the dates on open cartons during the opening checks.
If-it-fails: Throw the milk away and write it in the diary.
Supplied-text:
EH-review:
State: confirmed
By: Priya Shah
On: 2026-11-17

## OWN-02 Sous vide eggs

Kind: special-process
Process: sous vide
Hazard: Sous vide eggs are cooked at a low temperature, so harmful bacteria could survive if they are not cooked exactly as the method says.
Control: We cook sous vide eggs only by our written method, below.
Limit:
Limit-source:
Check: Each morning the water bath's own thermometer is checked against the probe thermometer.
If-it-fails: Eggs not cooked by the method are thrown away, and the water bath is not used until it is checked.
Supplied-text: Our sous vide egg method, written with our equipment supplier.
  We cook British Lion eggs in their shells, in a covered water bath.
  The bath is set and checked to the time and temperature in the supplier's instructions before any eggs go in.
  Eggs are served straight away and never kept for later.
EH-review: pending
State: confirmed
By: Sam Okafor
On: 2026-11-17
Source:
